text:
Jenna: FYI support ticket from Carlos (acme-inc) — they saw a sudden burst of 429s this morning and an unexpected invoice line for burst usage. Can eng-sre take a look?

Carlos: Seeing ~20% 429 rate between 08:14-08:28 UTC, then a big billing jump. We haven't changed traffic. Attaching request ids and sample traces.

Jenna: sample traces: req ids xYz123, xYz124, xYz127. Also saw limiter logs showing refills happening twice around the same timestamps.

Raj: grabbing logs now. Which limiter variant are they on — per-tenant shard or global?

Maya: ACME is on per-tenant sharded limiter (3 shards). We recently rolled a config change to add a window_offset_ms to spread refills. Could be related.

Raj: @Maya can you paste the exact config that rolled?

Maya: here's the deployed snippet (from k8s config):

```
rate_limiter:
  algorithm: token_bucket
  capacity: 1200
  refill_amount: 1200
  refill_interval_ms: 60000
  shards: 3
  window_offset_ms: 0
```

Maya: The change added window_offset_ms to try to avoid simultaneous refills, but it looks like on some nodes the offset was applied incorrectly and multiple shards ended up with the same offset (0) due to race in the config bootstrap.

Raj: Ok that explains overlapping refills across shards — tokens effectively doubled for a short period when offsets aligned, allowing burst drain and then sudden exhaustion and 429s after. Need repro/logs.

alert-bot: [incident] rate-limiter-refill-anomaly detected for tenant acme-inc (spike score 8.4) at 2024-11-09T08:21:13Z.

Raj: Collected node logs. Sample from shard-1:

```
[2024-11-09T08:20:00.001Z] refill: +1200 tokens (window_start=1700000400000)
[2024-11-09T08:20:00.002Z] refill: +1200 tokens (window_start=1700000400000)
```

Raj: And shard-2 shows same window_start at same ms — they shouldn't. Also noticed system clocks on two pods were within 1ms — causing rollout bootstrap to pick same offset.

Priya: If leader-election isn't used for offset assignment we can get collisions. Short term: force offsets to be randomized at runtime and add jitter.

Maya: Immediate mitigation options: 1) force per-tenant capacity to a conservative value (lower capacity) for acme, 2) roll back the window_offset change, 3) restart rate-limiter pods to pick new offsets. What do we want to do now?

Jenna: Customer is impacted, recommend fastest approach that fixes errors asap. Carlos, you ok with a brief throttle reduction while we stabilize?

Carlos: Yes, do whatever reduces 429s quickly — keep us posted. We need billing rectified afterwards.

Raj: I think restart pods + emergency policy to cap effective capacity to 600 for tenant acme is fastest. Restart will cause temporary small disruption but helps offsets re-randomize. I'll apply cap via API now.

Raj: Command I'm running: 
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme-inc/policy -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_API' -d '{"max_capacity":600}'
```

Maya: K8s restart next: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/rate-limiter -n infra` — doing that in canary then cluster.

alert-bot: [deploy] rollout of rate-limiter started at 2024-11-09T08:25:12Z by Maya.

Raj: Cap applied. Monitoring 1m.

Maya: Canary pods restarted, offsets randomized. Observability shows refill alignment gone for canary.

Jenna: Carlos reports 429s dropping to <1% after 08:27 UTC.

Carlos: Confirmed — errors back to normal. Thanks. Please advise on billing credits.

Priya: I'll loop in billing. For root cause we should: (1) revert the deterministic offset assignment logic, (2) enforce leader-election when computing offsets, (3) add monotonic-clock check and jitter, (4) add e2e test to validate offsets do not collide across shards.

Raj: Agreed. Also adding alert when >1 refill event with same window_start for same tenant observed across shards within 5ms — that's our indicator.

Maya: Proposed longterm patch: replace naive offset seed with per-pod /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid plus monotonic-ns + pod-uid and run leader-election fallback. I'll open PR.

Jenna: For customer remediation: suggest refunding the burst charges and a 1-month credit for inconvenience. @Priya can you confirm?

Priya: Confirming — will submit billing credit request and include incident summary. Also will update the SLA note.

Raj: Post-incident actions I've added to the incident board: 
- hotfix merged to remove deterministic offset (PR#4321)
- implement jitter + leader-election (PR#4322)
- add integration test in staging that creates 10 shards and checks no refill timestamp collisions for 10m
- add alert rule for refill-collision
- runbook update for restart + emergency cap

Maya: Timeline to full rollout: hotfix -> canary tomorrow morning -> full roll within 48h after canary metrics look good.

Carlos: Thanks team. Please share final postmortem and billing actions.

Jenna: Will draft postmortem and share by EOD.

Priya: I'll kick off billing request and notify customer success.

Raj: Closing immediate incident. Leaving this thread open for postmortem comments.

alert-bot: [incident-closed] rate-limiter-refill-anomaly for acme-inc closed at 2024-11-09T09:00:00Z.
